objective: Define tunnel close, drain and reconnect outcomes: transport loss remains separate from authoritative domain refusal.

decision.terminal_authority: Only a generated gRPC call that observes the server terminal status/trailers has an authoritative domain outcome. A WebSocket or HTTP/2 closure before that terminal is a transport outcome, even when the peer received the request.
decision.drain: The caller may close after consuming terminal gRPC trailers and releasing streams. Existing native pump selects the first completed direction; a WebSocket Close during an active RPC does not promise continued response draining.
decision.reconnect: A fresh BrowserConnection owns a new WebSocket/h2 driver, callback queue and BrowserChannel. Old connection callbacks/queues are released; a lost call is not automatically replayed. An external operation-ID query/resync is needed to resolve possible committed effects.
decision.classification: The executable fixture compares exact terminal metadata/status with the transport Status error source, actual closed connection owner and server-side forced-loss witness. Code text alone is not the classifier.

alternatives.choice: Keep current public NativeAdmission/TunnelStream and BrowserConnection/BrowserChannel; add fixture-only close/loss probes
alternatives.reason: The existing generated Tonic client and h2 adapter remain the only wire and authority path.

alternatives.rejected: Treat clean WebSocket Close as successful RPC drain
alternatives.reason: The current native pump stops the other byte direction when close wins, and an active RPC may lack terminal trailers.

alternatives.rejected: Automatically replay an uncertain mutating call after reconnect
alternatives.reason: The current fixture has no durable operation-ID lookup; replay could duplicate a committed effect.

alternatives.rejected: Classify errors by gRPC code or status-message substring alone
alternatives.reason: HTTP/2 errors can map to ordinary gRPC codes and messages are not authority evidence.

executable_cases.native_idle_close: Real loopback WebSocket through public NativeIncoming/TunnelStream; blocked read wakes at EOF, all pipe owners release.
executable_cases.native_partial_close: Real partial HTTP/2 preface over WebSocket; close yields UnexpectedEof and rejected transport, blocked read wakes and owners release.
executable_cases.browser_domain_refusal: Real generated client receives InvalidArgument, exact fixture-terminal trailer, no transport error source.
executable_cases.browser_afterdrain_close: Generated unary and server stream complete with terminal trailers before BrowserConnection::close; callback owners release.
executable_cases.browser_forced_loss: Real generated Wait RPC dispatches into native Tonic fixture; native WebSocket is forced closed before terminal; browser sees transport source/no domain trailer plus exact peer loss witness.
executable_cases.browser_reconnect: Fresh BrowserConnection executes a new generated unary while old connection stays closed with no queued callback and no replay of Wait.
